description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Joern fixture that carries one finding whose bytecode class key is claimed by two distinct source files by the both_schemes_in_test_trees route, so no unique resolution exists to take. One of three documents that reach ambiguous_source_resolution, one per route; ambiguity_route_policy names all three and states what each shows that the others do not. Every value was derived by reading the fixture against the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/ and by resolving the class key against a source index measured over the pinned tree; the adapter was run afterwards, to corroborate. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. The key names are the ones expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json established and expected/derived-joern-features.rows.json extends -- the shared metadata keys, the three parts rows / row_derivations / rejections, and the negative-only additions routing, rejection_boundary, rejections and counts.parse_status -- so one generic loader reads every expected file in this tree.
scanner_class_authority: AAP 0.5.4's class table fixes sast for opengrep, semgrep, datadog-static-analyzer and joern. The value is fixed in advance rather than derived from what the artifact turns out to contain, and it is identical on every row. Trivy is the single tool whose scanner_class varies by record, and joern is not it.
artifact_shape_note: This is the only artifact whose shape is the harness's own collector output rather than a tool-native format. There is no Joern output format to look up: harness/bin/run-joern.sh loads the code-property graph with importCpg, runs the bounded query set baked into harness/lib/joern-scan.sc, and that script writes the artifact itself.
no_user_rules_govern_this_file: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', and that single line is the complete document. No rule is cited here and none is invented, corroborated by AAP 0.7 and AAP 0.10.2. Enterprise best practice applies in their place, held to the AAP's own bar: hand-verify from the fixture rather than from a run, verify independently of the thing verified, and reject rather than infer.

fixture.shape: the collector shape the specification documents
fixture.finding_members_note: That is the union across the four records. path is present on 2 of them and absent on /findings/0 and /findings/2, which is load-bearing in two different directions and is stated per record under rejections and row_derivations rather than averaged away here.
fixture.derivation: A negative fixture is derived from captured output rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated as a derivation. Two things are derived and nothing else is invented. First the shape: the raw artifact is written in this provisioning's collector shape, and every record here is re-spelled into the documented shape -- query_id becomes rule_id, class becomes class_file, the severity label is dropped, and the collector's own path and path_resolution members are supplied. Second, one of the four coordinates is a class key that two distinct source files in the pinned tree really do claim, which is what this document exists to assert. The coordinates, their method signatures and their reported lines are values of the kind the raw artifact carries, and the collision is reproducible against the checkout rather than staged. This document was then derived from a six-finding predecessor by deleting the rows$ record and the SparkContext record; see fixture_split.
fixture.excerpt_note: The fixture is never edited to suit these rows; these rows are re-derived when the fixture changes. The recorded sha256 above is what makes an edit to it visible.
fixture.absolute_member_not_copied: The envelope carries a cpg_path member naming the graph file with an absolute path. It is deliberately not copied into this file, which stays free of absolute paths; the graph's identity is recorded elsewhere by byte size and sha256.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- SARIF is a version of "2.1.0" together with a runs array, and this document carries neither, so it is a native artifact routed by the runner that wrote it
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route("joern", doc) returns tool "joern", shape "native", adapter "joern", scanner_class "sast"
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No shape-detection failure is expected here, and a test asserting one against this fixture would be asserting the wrong thing. The enclosing document is a well-formed native Joern artifact and routes cleanly; one finding inside it is defective, and the adapter rejects that one while still emitting the other three. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py. A Joern artifact is eligible material for that assertion, but the assertion itself is not this file's and is not made here.
routing.caller_fault_is_not_a_rejection: normalize.adapters.joern.JoernAdapterError describes a defective call -- the wrong tool identifier, a relative root, another tool's path base, a path base whose kind is not bytecode_class, or a document that is not an object -- and stops the caller. None of those is in play here, and none is ever counted as a rejection: a caller fault absorbed into a rejection count would let a wrong root produce a plausible dataset for a whole tool.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant, which harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py restates as its own FIELDS because AAP 0.6.4 permits an adapter to import paths and severity and nothing else. The two were compared and are identical. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS. path in particular is not an optional field (AAP 0.5.4), which is why a record whose coordinate cannot be resolved uniquely is a counted rejection rather than a row with a null path.

rule_id_vocabulary.read_from: findings[].rule_id, the first candidate of the adapter's RULE_ID_FIELDS = ('rule_id', 'query_id'). Every one of the six records resolves its identifier there, so rule_id_from_rule_id counts 6 and rule_id_from_query_id counts 0 -- including the three rejected records, whose identifier resolves at step 2 before their path is examined at step 4.
rule_id_vocabulary.never_used_to_filter: joern.py's KNOWN_RULE_IDS carries these five together with the six identifiers harness/lib/joern-scan.sc bakes in this provisioning, and it is documentation and a cross-check only. AAP 0.4.2 has the baked bundle's actual composition read from the runner, so an identifier outside the set is a legitimate finding from a query set the constant predates, and dropping it would silently shrink a tool's count.
rule_id_vocabulary.no_query_to_finding_link: No rule_id is ever taken from a queries[].id. The documented queries[] carries only {id, count} and records no link between a query and a finding, so a match there would be inference; each finding names its own query through its own rule_id member.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.
allowlist.one_correction_worth_carrying: Neither claimant of this document's colliding key is in any of the twelve globs, and both contain the literal src/test besides, so a first-wins pick would have carried in_scope false either way. That does not make the pick harmless: the row would still have named one of two files, and the count of out-of-scope rows would have been one higher than the dataset can justify.

shape_divergence.summary: This fixture is written in the collector shape the specification documents, which is the opposite half of the divergence expected/joern.rows.json records: that fixture captures this provisioning's shape. The divergence itself is recorded, not repaired -- AAP 0.1.3's authority rule -- and the adapter reads both shapes in a fixed field precedence so the choice is reproducible.
shape_divergence.documented_shape: {tool, cpg_path, generated_at, cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size, declaration_index_size, queries: [{id, count}], findings: [{rule_id, message, path, start_line, method_full_name, class_file, path_resolution}]}
shape_divergence.provisioned_shape: {tool, tool_version, cpg, graph: {methods, type_declarations, files}, query_set, queries: [{id, bound, returned, bound_reached, elapsed_ms, callee_prefixes[]}], findings: [{query_id, severity, message, callee, class, method, file, line}]}
shape_divergence.the_collector_this_provisioning_actually: harness/lib/joern-scan.sc, 122 lines of Scala, verified present, which performs no source resolution at all: it emits the frontend's ephemeral extraction path in a file member the runner metadata names as the one to ignore. The AAP's cross-reference list names a Python collector under harness/lib/ that this provisioning does not carry -- verified absent -- so the documented shape is a contract this fixture carries rather than a file's output, and no behaviour is attributed to the absent file; see divergences_recorded. harness/lib/normalize/paths.py and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py both record the same divergence from their own side, which is why paths.class_key accepts either a dotted type full name or a class-file path.

differences.documented: findings[].class_file, a class-file path such as org/apache/spark/deploy/master/Master.class
differences.observed_here: findings[].class_file on all four records; no class member is present on any of them
differences.consequence: coordinate_from_class_file counts 4 and coordinate_from_class counts 0. The runner metadata names class as record_path_field, so the adapter tries it first and falls through to class_file, which is why a document in either shape resolves. normalize.paths.class_key accepts either form, so the precedence decides which member is read, never how it is interpreted.

differences.observed_here: no severity member at all -- the literal string severity does not occur anywhere in the fixture
differences.consequence: Every emitted row carries severity_native null and severity_norm Info on the no_vocabulary basis, so severity_absent counts 3 and severity_from_record_label counts 0.
differences.why_this_is_the_contract: AAP 0.5.4 places joern under 'No vocabulary at all (gitleaks; joern unless a query defines one) -- severity_native absent, severity_norm Info, the absence stated rather than a level assumed'. Here no query defines one, so the absence is stated. Info is never written by the adapter directly: severity.py owns the vocabulary, the precedence and the bands, so this file cannot disagree with severity-map.md.

differences.documented: findings[].path, the collector's own already-root-relative answer, and findings[].path_resolution, its explanation of how it got there
differences.observed_here: path_resolution on all four records; path on 2 of them, and absent on findings 0 and 2
differences.consequence: collector_explanation_present counts 4, because the counter is taken before the path step decides a record's outcome. Both records carrying a collector path are emitted rows whose own resolution the collector agrees with -- collector_path_corroborated 2 -- and the ambiguous record carries none, so collector_path_refused stays 0 for want of a candidate rather than by refusal.

differences.documented: flat cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size and declaration_index_size
differences.observed_here: all four present; no nested graph object
differences.consequence: envelope_graph_methods, envelope_graph_type_declarations, envelope_collector_source_index_size and envelope_collector_declaration_index_size all carry figures, while envelope_graph_files stays 0 because the nested object that would supply it is absent. The per-query tally is spelled count here rather than returned, and neither is summed into any published figure.

count_unit.per_query_tally_member: queries[].count in this shape; queries[].returned in the provisioned shape
count_unit.which_one_is_the_raw_count: len(findings) = 4. The sum of the per-query tallies is 593 -- 412 + 178 + 3 -- and is not the raw count and is not published as one.
count_unit.why_they_differ: The fixture carries four findings beside a queries[] array whose counts describe a whole scan. The two numbers therefore differ by construction, which is what makes the reconciliation assertion non-vacuous: an implementation that counted the per-query tallies instead of the findings would produce 593 against 3 rows and 1 rejection and fail loudly rather than agree silently.
count_unit.authority: AAP 0.5.4 makes findings[] the reconciliation unit, and normalize.reconcile.count_records walks that same unit without building rows. The adapter deliberately publishes no count of the findings it walked, so the left-hand side of the identity cannot be taken from the traversal that builds the right-hand side.

resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the joern entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.why_no_filesystem_base_exists: The runner queries a graph the frontend built over staged JARs rather than over the source tree, so a reported file member is by construction the frontend's extraction path for a .class member and can never be a path in the Spark tree. The metadata therefore records a null base value rather than inventing a plausible one, and the class coordinate is the only resolvable one. Because has_explicit_base is false, no metadata-backed fallback is available to this tool at all.
resolution_context.resolution_procedure: The class coordinate is reduced by normalize.paths.class_key to <package path>/<outer type name>, truncating the basename at its first $ so a companion object, an anonymous class and a nested class all collapse to the outer type. That key is then looked up in a source index over src/main and src/test under the pinned root, across two key schemes: by_filename on <package dir>/<file base name>, and by_decl on <package dir>/<declared type name>. The union of candidates must be exactly one distinct path.

index_measured_over_the_pinned_tree.note: This document's collision -- org/apache/spark/SparkContextSuite -- is in that list, and it is there only because the index spans src/test: both claimants are test files. The union route's key, org/apache/spark/SparkContext, is deliberately not in the list, because it is unique under by_filename and collides only once by_decl is included; a reader must not expect the list and the set of colliding keys the three documents carry to coincide.
index_measured_over_the_pinned_tree.reproduces_the_adapter_docstring: These six figures are the ones harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py records in its own docstring, measured again here rather than copied.

resolution_context.gap_1_closed: The index spans src/main and src/test rather than src/main alone. Every -tests artifact the build emitted is in the graph input, so a finding can legitimately name bytecode compiled from a test tree, and such a resolution is retained with in_scope false rather than dropped. Row 1 below is that case, and rows_from_src_test counts it.
resolution_context.gap_2_closed: A resolution is taken only where the union of candidates across both key schemes and both source trees is exactly one distinct path. Two or more is ambiguous_source_resolution with every competing candidate named, never a first-wins pick. The authority for the gap is harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py's own module docstring, under 'The two collector gaps, closed here', which states that the shape the AAP describes resolves such a collision first-wins in walk order and that this run declines to; harness/lib/normalize/paths.py records the same from the resolver's side. Nothing is attributed to a file this provisioning does not carry -- see divergences_recorded. No collector is edited either way: AAP 0.5.2 has no runner or harness helper modified, so the gap is closed in the adapter and nowhere else. Closing gap 1 increases ambiguity, which is why closing gap 2 is mandatory rather than optional -- and this document is that demonstration, since its collision is a pair of src/test files a src/main-only index would never have seen collide.
resolution_context.collector_path_precedence: Fixed by the adapter. This run's own unique class-to-source resolution governs; an ambiguous key is never overridden by the collector's answer; where this run resolves nothing and the collector did supply a root-relative path, that path is emitted as-is and marked uncorroborated; and where both resolve and differ, this run's answer is kept and the disagreement recorded. All three emitted rows take the first branch. The one rejected record takes the second, and it carries no collector path at all, so the refusal is unobservable on this route and is asserted on its two siblings instead; what this route asserts is that the class is decided by what this run's index found rather than by what the collector could not place.
resolution_context.root_dependence: These rows depend on a live tree: the class-to-source resolution reads the pinned checkout at $SPARK_SRC. Every emitted path is expressed relative to that root and none is absolute, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
resolution_context.severity_source: No record states a severity, and this shape has no rule object to fall back on, so every row takes severity.py's no-vocabulary path: severity_native null, severity_norm Info, basis no_vocabulary. The absence is stated rather than a level assumed.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A Joern finding names a bytecode call site rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry. The absence is explicitly not a rejection: the unformable_package_coordinate class covers a dependency-oriented record, and this shape is not one.

rejection_boundary.statement: An ambiguous coordinate is a rejection. A coordinate that resolves uniquely to somewhere unwanted is a kept row with in_scope false. This document's first record resolves to two distinct files, which is what makes it the ambiguous_source_resolution case; a later record resolves uniquely into a src/test tree and is a kept row, which is what makes the document able to tell the two apart.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: path is one of only two never-absent fields in the twelve-field schema, the other being severity_norm: emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS carries path, and emit.OPTIONAL_FIELDS is exactly severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve and package_coordinate. A record with two candidate paths has no single value to put in that field, and the three alternatives -- dropping it, picking one, or emitting both -- each either hide the record or invent a fact. Counting it under a named class is the only outcome that does neither.

not_a_rejection.case: a unique resolution into a src/test tree, from a -tests artifact in the graph input
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope and rows_from_src_test
not_a_rejection.evidence: AAP 0.5.4 requires a test-JAR finding kept out of scope rather than dropped, and AAP 0.9.3 repeats it among the recorded-not-halting conditions. The literal src/test exclusion lives in paths.in_scope and removes the path from scope, never from the dataset.

not_a_rejection.case: a resolution outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope
not_a_rejection.evidence: A class in a module the allowlist does not name resolves to a real file and is kept. Out of scope means kept and marked.
not_a_rejection.which_record: the same record: core/src/test/... matches no glob and is additionally caught by the literal src/test rule, so both readings agree on in_scope false

not_a_rejection.case: two candidates that are the same path reached through both key schemes
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row -- SourceIndex.candidates takes the union of distinct paths, so one file found twice is one candidate and not an ambiguity
not_a_rejection.evidence: All three emitted rows are that case: each resolves on basis source-index-filename+declaration, meaning both schemes contributed and both named the same file. An implementation that counted scheme hits rather than distinct paths would reject all three and this fixture would catch it.

rejection_boundary.no_guessed_path: The rejected record is rejected and counted, never given a path. Nothing in this file supplies a coordinate for it, not even one of the two candidates the index found.
rejection_boundary.and_the_collector_answer_is_refused: The rejected record carries no collector path, so there is no fallback to refuse on this route and collector_path_refused is 0 for want of a candidate rather than by refusal. The refusal itself is asserted on the two sibling routes, whose defective records each carry one. What this route asserts instead is that the absence of a collector answer does not change the class: two claimants make it ambiguous, not unresolvable.

collisions_verified_at_the_pin.note: One collision, verified against the pinned checkout rather than assumed. Its two sibling documents carry the other two collisions the predecessor held, and ambiguity_route_policy states what each shows: ambiguity is not one phenomenon, and the three fail in different ways.

collisions.why_it_collides: Two modules carry a test suite of the same name in the same package. Both files are named SparkContextSuite.scala and both declare the type, so both schemes name both paths and the union is two.
collisions.ambiguity_is_not_confined_to_main_trees: This is the case only gap 1 makes visible. A src/main-only index would hold neither candidate, so the record would have been unresolvable rather than ambiguous -- a different class, a different detail and a different diagnosis. Widening the index to src/test is what turns it into a collision, which is the concrete reason the adapter's docstring gives for closing gap 2 being mandatory once gap 1 is closed rather than optional.
collisions.both_candidates_are_out_of_scope: Both paths contain the literal src/test, so had either been picked the row would have carried in_scope false. That does not make the pick harmless: the row would still have named one of two files, and the count of out-of-scope rows would have been one higher than the dataset can justify.
collisions.fixture_record: /findings/0, which carries no collector path and whose path_resolution is unresolved-bytecode-only -- the collector could not place it either, and this run's own index finds two claimants

collisions_verified_at_the_pin.a_fourth_collision_exists_and_is_not_use: org/apache/spark/SparkConf collides through the same pair of files as the union-of-both-schemes route, via core's SparkConf.scala and the shims stub at line 20. It is named for completeness and deliberately not carried by any document: it would restate that route's mechanism without adding a distinct failure mode, and a fixture that repeats a case rather than adding one costs a reader time without buying coverage.

no_row_carries_a_colliding_candidate.assertion: No emitted row's path is any of the six candidate paths the three collisions name, and no colliding candidate appears anywhere in the rows array in any field.
no_row_carries_a_colliding_candidate.why_it_must_be_asserted_separately: A buggy adapter could both reject a record and emit a row for it -- rejecting on the ambiguity while a second code path emitted the collector's answer, say -- and every other assertion in this file would still pass: the rejection count would be right, the class would be right, and the row count would merely be higher than the identity allows. The identity raw = rows + rejections would catch a duplicate emission in this fixture, but only because no other record is missing; asserting the paths directly catches it whatever else changes.
no_row_carries_a_colliding_candidate.why_the_list_spans_the_whole_route_famil: Six paths for one collision, on purpose. The three documents carry the same three sound records and therefore the same three rows, so no row in any of them may name any claimant of any of the three colliding keys -- and the same list can be asserted against all three. Narrowing it to this document's own two claimants would weaken the assertion for no gain: a wrong row naming a sibling route's candidate would then pass.
no_row_carries_a_colliding_candidate.method: Exact comparison against every row's path field, and substring comparison against every field of every row -- not inspection by eye. The three emitted paths are Master.scala, MasterSuite.scala and UdfPacket.scala, none of which is a candidate above; note that Master.scala and MasterSuite.scala differ from one another only by a suffix, so the comparison has to be on the full path rather than on a simple name.
no_row_carries_a_colliding_candidate.and_no_partial_emission: The rejected record contributes to no per-row counter either: path_kind_bytecode_source is 3 rather than 4, severity_absent is 3, start_line_from_start_line is 3, and rows_in_scope plus rows_out_of_scope is 3. A record that had half-emitted would show up as an asymmetry there.

contrast_row.why_it_earns_its_place: Without it, an implementation that rejected every test-tree path -- or every path whose simple name looks like it might have a twin in another module -- would pass this fixture while discarding the legitimate -tests findings AAP 0.5.4 requires kept. The fixture would then assert 'reject the ambiguous' and accidentally also accept 'reject the inconvenient', which are not the same instruction. This row is the one that separates them.
contrast_row.it_is_also_the_gap_1_proof: MasterSuite.class has no candidate under src/main at all; it resolves only because the index spans src/test as well. So the row demonstrates gap 1 being closed, while the rejected record beside it demonstrates the ambiguity that closing gap 1 introduces. One document, both halves of the same design decision.
contrast_row.and_it_is_a_unique_resolution: Exactly one file in either tree claims org/apache/spark/deploy/master/MasterSuite, which is why it is a row and not a rejection -- worth stating because a neighbouring key is not unique: org/apache/spark/SparkContextSuite is claimed by both core and hadoop-cloud, and it is this document's own rejected record. The two keys differ only in the type name, so nothing about the path shape decides the outcome; only the candidate count does.
contrast_row.cross_file_agreement: expected/joern.rows.json's row 7 resolves the same coordinate from the provisioned shape's class member and reaches the same path, the same start_line 218, the same in_scope false and the same 252-line anchor. The two expected files were derived independently and agree. They differ in exactly two fields and both differences are by design rather than disagreement: rule_id is joern.reflective-class-load here and joern-reflection-forname there, because the two shapes carry different query identifiers, and severity is null/Info here against MEDIUM/Medium there, because that shape's records state a label and this one's state none.

rejection_pair.this_half: ambiguous -- too much found. Two or more distinct source files claim one class key, so no unique coordinate exists to take, and the class is paths.REJECT_AMBIGUOUS_SOURCE_RESOLUTION. Reached by three routes, one per committed document; see ambiguity_route_policy.
rejection_pair.sibling_half: unresolvable -- nothing found. The class key has zero candidates, so no coordinate exists at all, and the class is paths.REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH.
rejection_pair.why_each_needs_its_own_diagnosis: Both are rejections and both leave the record out of the dataset, so a test that only counted rejections could not tell them apart -- which is why the class name is what carries the assertion. They differ in three ways that matter. The class differs, so tool-status.md attributes them to different conditions. The detail differs: this one names every competing candidate, while the sibling names the simple name, the package searched and both source trees. And the collector fallback differs, which is the sharpest of the three: for an unresolvable coordinate the collector's own root-relative path is used where it supplied one, while for an ambiguous key it is never used to break the tie.
rejection_pair.opposite_reasons_note: Nothing found and too much found are opposite failures of the same requirement -- that a resolution be taken only where it is unique -- so covering one does not cover the other, and neither fixture makes the other redundant.
rejection_pair.the_sibling_reserved_this_case_for_here: expected/reject-joern-unresolvable-path.rows.json states under ambiguous_case_reserved_for_the_sibling that rows.scala is deliberately absent from its fixture and names the ambiguity fixture as the cover. The reservation holds in fact: the literal rows occurs nowhere in that fixture, and reject-joern-ambiguous-path.json carries rows.scala, rows$ and rows$.class.

ambiguity_route_policy.statement: One rejection class, three committed documents. ambiguous_source_resolution is reached wherever the union of candidates across both key schemes and both source trees is two or more distinct paths, and the way a key comes to have two claimants differs in kind rather than in degree. The class name is identical on all three and the route is named only in the detail's candidate list, so a test asserting the class alone would pass against any of them.
ambiguity_route_policy.why_one_document_per_route: AAP 0.9.4 requires a negative fixture and an assertion for every rejection condition an exercised adapter can produce. One document carrying all three collisions satisfies the class but not the conditions: its rejection count is three, no assertion can name which collision it is asserting, and a regression that broke exactly one route would leave the count unchanged in two of the three ways it could fail. One attributable case per document is what makes each route's assertion falsifiable.

the_three_routes.resolution_scheme: filename only -- by_decl holds no entry for this key, because neither file declares a type named rows
the_three_routes.what_only_this_route_shows: That a first-wins pick would decide two fields rather than one. The two claimants declare disjoint type sets and carry opposite in_scope values, so picking either names a file declaring none of the other's types and settles scope by accident.

the_three_routes.resolution_scheme: the union only -- by_filename holds exactly one candidate and by_decl holds two
the_three_routes.what_only_this_route_shows: That the resolution is the union of both schemes rather than a precedence between them. It is the one route a plausible wrong implementation resolves, so it is the route that separates a correct adapter from one that merely orders its lookups.

the_three_routes.resolution_scheme: both -- each scheme names both candidates
the_three_routes.what_only_this_route_shows: That ambiguity is not confined to main trees, and that the class is decided by what this run's index found rather than by what the collector failed to find: the defective record carries no collector path at all and is still the ambiguous class rather than the unresolvable one.

ambiguity_route_policy.what_is_identical_across_the_three: The same envelope, the same three sound records and therefore the same three rows in the same order, and the same 43 counter values. The three documents differ in exactly one findings[] element -- the defective one at index 0 -- which is what makes the rejection the only thing under test.
ambiguity_route_policy.what_is_not_a_route: A key with three or more claimants is not a fourth route: the detail reports the count rather than assuming two, so a larger candidate list is the same code path. All four ambiguous by_filename keys measured at the pin have exactly two claimants, so a three-way collision is not available from this checkout without synthesizing one.
ambiguity_route_policy.the_class_is_final_on_every_route: On all three routes the ambiguity is final: normalize.adapters.joern._resolve_path returns the ambiguous rejection immediately and never consults the collector's own path member. That is the difference from every other path rejection this adapter can produce, where the collector's path is tried as a fallback before the rejection stands -- and it is why no route can be rescued by a fallback, whether or not the defective record happens to carry one.
ambiguity_route_policy.authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py's module docstring, under 'The two collector gaps, closed here', and harness/lib/normalize/paths.py's resolve_bytecode_class, whose ambiguity branch returns before any fallback is considered. Read from those modules rather than inferred from the fixtures.

fixture_split.what_changed: This document and its two named siblings were one fixture carrying three ambiguities and one expected file recording three rejections under one name.
fixture_split.why: A fixture assigned one attributable case yielded three, so its name, its expected reject class and its expected count did not agree, and no assertion could name which collision it was asserting. The earlier revision of this file recorded the mismatch as a divergence and left it standing; recording a defect is not resolving one.
fixture_split.how: Textual derivation from the six-finding predecessor: two whole findings[] elements were dropped from each output and nothing else was touched. The envelope, the whole queries array and every kept finding are byte-identical to the predecessor's, and each kept finding was compared as a parsed object rather than by eye. No JSON round-trip was used -- the predecessor carries compact one-line queries[] and findings[] entries inside an indented envelope, and re-serializing would have rewritten every byte of it.

the_three_documents.dropped_from_the_predecessor: the SparkContext record and the SparkContextSuite record
the rows$ record and the SparkContextSuite record
the rows$ record and the SparkContext record

fixture_split.nothing_in_the_adapter_changed_for_this: No file under harness/lib/normalize/ was edited. The adapter produced three rejections from the predecessor because the predecessor carried three defective records, and it produces one from each of these because each carries one. The split is a change to the corpus, not to the code under test.
fixture_split.coverage_is_not_reduced: All three collisions the predecessor carried are still committed, one per document, and each is now asserted by name through its own route and its own distinguishing substrings. Reducing to a single ambiguity would have deleted two genuine routes, including the only one a precedence-based resolver would silently resolve.

divergences_recorded.this_provisioning_has: harness/lib/joern-scan.sc, 122 lines of Scala, verified present, which performs no source resolution at all: it emits the frontend's ephemeral extraction path in a file member the runner metadata names as the one to ignore. The Python collector the cross-reference list names is absent -- verified absent.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of findings[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records("joern", doc), whose traversal takes the length of the findings array and builds no row, resolves no path and maps no severity. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing. Measured on this fixture, it returns 4.
counts.one_finding_one_outcome: Structural rather than asserted: the adapter's per-finding function returns a single value that is either a row or a rejection, so there is no path that emits both and none that emits neither. len(rows) + len(rejections) therefore equals the number of findings[] elements walked by construction -- which is also what makes no_row_carries_a_colliding_candidate an assertion about a second code path rather than about this one.

four_reported_counters.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- the four counts reported per tool
four_reported_counters.values_live_in: counters, for the two this adapter publishes, and aap_reported_counters for all four with the reason each is what it is

counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = "partial", assigned as partial where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: every parsable record was emitted and each rejected record is counted under its class with its reason retained. This is deliberately not normalize.reconcile's STATUS_PASS / STATUS_FAIL / STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE vocabulary, which describes an assertion's outcome rather than an artifact's parse.
counts.not_applicable_is_a_different_case: An artifact that was never written reconciles as not applicable -- artifact absent, not as zero equals zero. That case belongs to osv-scanner, which wrote nothing, and it is not this fixture's.
counts.one_of_four_records_is_rejected_and_that: One of four is a property of a document built to isolate one condition, not a rate to read as a defect. The production artifact's own proportion is different and is recorded where it belongs, in tool-status.md, from that artifact rather than from this one.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): 43 keys -- 23 authored, 5 envelope integers, one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member, one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member, and one provenance key per member of each field-candidate tuple. The keys above are in COUNTER_KEYS order and the set is complete: every key the adapter initialises appears, so a zero here means measured-zero rather than not-measured.
counters_note: Five things a reader must not 'correct'. First, the per-finding counters split 4 / 3: rule_id_from_rule_id, coordinate_from_class_file and collector_explanation_present all count 4 because every record reaches the rule step, the coordinate step and the explanation tally before the path step decides its outcome, while the severity, start_line, path_kind and in_scope counters all count 3 because only three records become rows. That asymmetry is the classification order made visible, not a miscount. Second, collector_path_refused is 0 and the rejected record carries no collector path, so on this route the zero records the absence of a candidate rather than a refusal; the refusal is asserted on the two sibling routes. Third, collector_path_corroborated is 2 rather than 3 -- rows 0 and 2 carry a collector path identical to this run's resolution, and row 1's record carries no path member at all, so there was nothing to corroborate it with. Fourth, source_index_supplied is 0, recording that the adapter built the index over the pinned root rather than being handed one; harness/lib/normalize/cli.py injects a prebuilt index over the same root in the production run, which moves exactly this one key to 1 and leaves the other six source_index_* figures and every row and rejection unchanged. Fifth, envelope_graph_files is 0 while the four other envelope figures carry values: this shape has no nested graph object, so the member that would supply a file count is absent, and 0 here means absent rather than a graph with no files.

aap_reported_counters.note: AAP 0.5.4 has four counters reported per tool. Two are members of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS and two are not, and the reason the two are absent is structural rather than an omission.

multi_location_records.basis: No finding in this shape carries a locations array; each names exactly one call site through its class coordinate, its method and its line. The counter is published anyway, so that a future collector emitting several locations is visible rather than silently reduced to its first.

non_filesystem_paths.basis: All three emitted paths have kind bytecode_source, which normalize.paths.is_non_filesystem_kind excludes -- only outside_root and archive_member are non-filesystem coordinates. Each names a real file in the pinned tree. The rejected record contributes to no path_kind_* counter at all, because it produced no row.

multi_valued_cwe_records.basis: Not a member of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS; the SARIF adapter publishes it because a SARIF rule can carry several CWE tokens. A Joern finding names a bytecode call site rather than a weakness catalogue entry, so cwe is null on every row by contract and the count is structurally 0. Manufacturing a CWE from a class name or a query identifier would be inference.

multi_valued_cve_records.basis: Not a member of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS, for the same reason: this shape carries no advisory identifier, so cve is null on every row by contract and the count is structurally 0.

envelope_fields.note: The envelope members outside findings[] are not findings and produce no rows. They must not appear in any row, and a twelve-key row makes that structural. They are recorded here because they are the figures a reader checks the artifact's provenance against, and a number that reaches no channel reaches no document.
envelope_fields.graph_figures_agree_with_the_run_record: The method and type-declaration figures are the ones recorded for the graph this run queried, so a fixture whose envelope disagreed with them would be a fixture built against a different graph. They are carried as evidence of provenance and are compared, never summed into a record count.
envelope_fields.collector_index_sizes_do_not_match_this_: source_index_size 4127 and declaration_index_size 9947 are the collector's own reported index sizes, and they are smaller than this run's independently measured 6759 files and 15230 declaration keys. The difference is the expected consequence of gap 1: a src/main-only index over the pinned tree is smaller than one spanning src/main and src/test. Recording both is the point -- reconciling them would erase the evidence that the two indexes are not the same index.
envelope_fields.cpg_path_member: The envelope carries a cpg_path member naming the graph file. It is an absolute path in the artifact and is deliberately not copied into this file, which stays free of absolute paths; the graph's identity is recorded elsewhere by byte size and sha256.
envelope_fields.generated_at_member: Carried by the fixture and deliberately not asserted here: it is a timestamp, it reaches no dataset field, and pinning it would make this file fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the adapter.
envelope_fields.bound_reached: This shape's queries[] carries only {id, count} and no bound_reached flag, so no query can report reaching a traversal bound and the counter is 0. That is the flag being absent rather than a query being known untruncated, and the two are not the same claim.

independent_derivation.method: Every field of every row, the rejection's class and its detail, and all 43 counter values were derived by reading the fixture against the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/ -- emit.FIELDS for the field set and order, paths.REJECT_CLASSES for the class name, the adapter's documented five-step classification order for which step each record is decided at, and severity.py's no-vocabulary path for the severity triple. The four class keys were reduced by hand under class_key's documented first-$ truncation, and each was looked up against a source index measured over the pinned tree; every candidate path was then confirmed to exist in the checkout, with its line count and its declarations read from the file itself.
independent_derivation.index_measurement: 6759 files indexed, 6755 by_filename keys of which 4 are ambiguous, and 15230 by_decl keys of which 107 are ambiguous -- reproducing the figures the adapter's own docstring records.

adapter_run.when: after the hand derivation, never before it
adapter_run.note: Running the adapter over this fixture with the recorded runner metadata and the pinned root reproduces all twelve fields of all three rows, the rejection's class, its full detail string, its record identity and all 43 counter values. That is corroboration recorded after the fact, not the source of these values.

positive_sibling.agreement: complete on the ten fields the two shapes share

negative_sibling.note: That file records the rows.scala collision under ambiguous_case_reserved_for_the_sibling with the same two candidate paths, the same 51 and 182 line counts, the same declarations and the same 167 for GenericInternalRow, and states that it reserved the case for the ambiguity fixture. Two files derived independently from the same checkout agree on it.

real_artifact.note: That artifact produces 585 rejections, every one under unresolvable_path, and no ambiguous_source_resolution rejection at all -- so this condition is one the production artifact does not happen to exercise. AAP 0.6.2 requires the negative fixture regardless: a rejection path with no test is a rejection path nobody has exercised, and the class is reachable for any bytecode class whose key two source files claim. This fixture is that test.

rows.message: rpc handler reaches driver launch site in bytecode

row_derivations_note: One entry per row, in row order, and the row order is the fixture's document order with the rejected record removed -- the rows are findings 1, 2 and 3, because the defective record is finding 0. Each entry names the fixture member every field was read from, the class key the coordinate reduced to, which index scheme resolved it, and the allowlist glob the path matched. file_line_count_at_the_pin is the resolved file's real length in the pinned checkout, which is what makes each start_line checkable rather than merely plausible.

row_derivations.severity_absent_reason: the finding carries no severity member, and this shape has no rule object to fall back on, so severity.py's no-vocabulary path applies: severity_native null with severity_norm Info and the absence stated rather than a level assumed
row_derivations.class_key_note: The .class suffix is stripped and the basename carries no $, so the key is the package path and the type name unchanged.
row_derivations.candidates_note: Both schemes name the same single file, so the union of distinct paths is one and the resolution is unique. Two scheme hits are not two candidates -- SourceIndex.candidates takes a set union -- and an implementation that confused the two would reject all three of these rows.
row_derivations.collector_path_agreement: identical to this run's unique resolution, so the record is counted under collector_path_corroborated and the collector's answer changes nothing about the row
row_derivations.collector_explanation_destination: no dataset field -- the record produced a row, and a row has nowhere to put it
row_derivations.scope_reason: in scope: matched the allowlist glob core/src/main/**
row_derivations.anchor_note: Line 417 of the pinned Master.scala is `val driver = createDriver(description)` in the RequestSubmitDriver branch of receiveAndReply, which is the call site the message names; the same call appears at 1130 and its definition at 1356. The file is 1436 lines, so start_line is within it.

row_derivations.purpose: The contrast row this fixture cannot do without. See contrast_row for why it earns its place and what it would cost to lose it.
row_derivations.class_key_note: The coordinate is the outer type already; the record's method_full_name names the synthetic $anonfun$new$29, and it is context in a rejection rather than a coordinate, so nothing is read from it here.
row_derivations.candidates_note: Exactly one file in either tree claims this key. The neighbouring key org/apache/spark/SparkContextSuite is claimed by two, and both keys name a test suite in a test tree -- so nothing about the shape of the path decides the outcome, only the candidate count does. That neighbouring key is this document's own rejected record.
row_derivations.collector_path_consequence: The record carries no path member, so there is nothing to corroborate this run's resolution with and collector_path_corroborated does not count it. The row is unaffected: this run's own unique resolution is what reaches the row in every case, and the collector's answer is only ever read to corroborate or to fall back on.
row_derivations.collector_explanation_destination: no dataset field. Worth stating plainly: the collector said it could not place this class, and this run placed it uniquely. The row is emitted on this run's resolution and the collector's admission reaches nothing -- it is retained only in a rejection, and this record is not one.
row_derivations.scope_reason: out of scope: the path contains the literal src/test. No glob matches core/src/test/... in any case, and the literal exclusion would override a positive glob match if one existed -- normalize.paths.in_scope applies that rule before consulting the globs. The row is retained and counted under rows_from_src_test and rows_out_of_scope.
row_derivations.anchor_note: Line 218 of the pinned MasterSuite.scala sits inside the test opened at line 215 and is an assertion calling invokePrivate, scalatest's reflective private-method accessor -- consistent with the reflective-class-load identifier the record carries. The file is 252 lines, so start_line is within it and no start_line above 252 is possible for this path.

row_derivations.class_key_note: The basename is truncated at its first $, so the companion object UdfPacket$ collapses to the outer type UdfPacket -- the same reduction that makes finding 0's rows$ reduce to rows, which is how a synthetic name reaches a source file at all.
row_derivations.collector_path_agreement: identical to this run's unique resolution, counted under collector_path_corroborated
row_derivations.scope_reason: in scope: matched the allowlist glob sql/connect/**/src/main/**, which requires a ** that means zero-or-more directories -- common is the one directory the mid-path ** absorbs here
row_derivations.anchor_note: Line 61 of the pinned UdfPacket.scala is `ois.readObject().asInstanceOf[UdfPacket]` inside `object UdfPacket`'s apply(in: InputStream), opened at line 59, with the ObjectInputStream constructed on line 60 -- the deserialization entry point the message names. The file is 71 lines, so start_line is within it. This row also shows the adapter carrying on past the three rejections rather than stopping at the first.

fields_absent_on_every_row.severity_native: No record carries a severity member and this shape has no rule object to fall back on, so the no-vocabulary path applies to all three rows. severity_norm is Info and is never absent.
fields_absent_on_every_row.cwe: A Joern finding names a bytecode call site, not a weakness catalogue entry, and this shape carries no CWE member. Deriving one from a query identifier would be inference.
fields_absent_on_every_row.cve: The same: this shape carries no advisory identifier.
fields_absent_on_every_row.package_coordinate: The same, and the absence is explicitly not a rejection here -- unformable_package_coordinate covers a dependency-oriented record, which this is not.

members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.note: Each of these is present in the fixture and must not appear in any row. Checked by substring comparison against every field of every row above, not merely by inspection.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.path_resolution: The collector's own explanation of how it resolved -- or failed to resolve -- a class, one of source-index-filename, source-index-declaration or unresolved-bytecode-only. AAP 0.5.4 confines it to the rejection record: 'any collector explanation for an unmappable bytecode path is retained in the rejection record, not in a dataset field.' It is diagnostic metadata, not data. Two of the three literals occur in this fixture -- source-index-filename on 2 records and unresolved-bytecode-only on 2 -- and neither occurs anywhere in the rows array.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.method_full_name: The enclosing method's full signature, present on all four records. Carried into a rejection's identity as diagnosable context, never into a row -- and never into message, however readable it looks.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.collector_path_on_a_rejected_record: findings[0] carries no path member, so there is no collector answer to keep out of the rows on this route. The two sibling documents each carry one and assert its absence from their rows; here the corresponding assertion is that the class is ambiguous rather than unresolvable despite the collector having placed nothing.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.envelope_members: tool, cpg_path, generated_at, cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size, declaration_index_size and queries are envelope metadata: not findings, and they produce no rows.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.collector_path_is_the_exception_that_is_: findings[].path can reach the path field, but only as a value the adapter emits as-is where this run's own resolution produces nothing unique -- and on this fixture it never does that. The record whose resolution failed failed by ambiguity, which refuses the fallback outright, and the three that resolved used their own resolution. So no row's path came from the collector here, which the counters record as collector_path_refused 0.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and finding_index name the same record. finding_index is carried as well because normalize.adapters.joern puts exactly that key into the rejection's record_identity, so a produced Rejection and this expectation can be compared directly without translating one coordinate system into the other. It is the native-shape equivalent of the run_index / result_index pair the SARIF expectations carry. The defective record is the document's first finding and the three sound records follow it, which is a consequence of deriving this document by deleting whole findings rather than by reordering them.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_AMBIGUOUS_SOURCE_RESOLUTION constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten. Written verbatim rather than paraphrased, and asserted against the module rather than by eye: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another, so the class name is what carries the assertion.
rejections.route_note: Both schemes hold both candidates, and the collision exists at all only because the index spans src/test as well as src/main. Under a src/main-only index this key has zero claimants and the record would be an unresolvable_path rejection instead -- a different class, a different detail and a different diagnosis. This is the route that shows closing gap 1 creating the ambiguity closing gap 2 has to handle.
rejections.classification_step: step 4 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. Steps 1 to 3 all pass on this record: it is a JSON object, it carries the non-empty rule identifier joern.reflective-class-load, and it carries a non-empty message. That is deliberate, so the only thing left to reject it for is its path.
rejections.start_line_never_examined: Step 5 is never reached, so this record's start_line of 42 is never examined and non_integer_start_line is not in play. Worth stating because the fixture does give the defective record a start_line, and it is a plausible line rather than an obviously wrong one -- exactly the kind of plausibility a reader should not read as corroboration of a coordinate the adapter refused to pick.
rejections.class_key_note: The coordinate is the outer type already and the basename carries no $, so the key is the package path and the type name unchanged.
rejections.candidate_order: The detail lists candidates in the order SourceIndex.candidates returns them, which is sorted, so the string is stable across runs and across filesystem walk orders. core sorts before hadoop-cloud.
rejections.resolution_scheme: both -- each scheme names both candidates
rejections.collector_path_consequence: There is none to refuse. The collector reported unresolved-bytecode-only and supplied no path, which is consistent with a src/main-only resolver: it could not place the class at all. The record is still rejected under the ambiguous class rather than the unresolvable one, because the class describes what this run's index found -- two claimants -- and not what the collector failed to find. Attributing it to the collector's reason would misclassify it.
rejections.collector_explanation_destination: the rejection's detail, appended as the suffix '; collector path_resolution: unresolved-bytecode-only'. It is not a record_identity key and it is not a dataset field.
rejections.expected_detail: the class key 'org/apache/spark/SparkContextSuite' is claimed by 2 distinct source files (core/src/test/scala/org/apache/spark/SparkContextSuite.scala, hadoop-cloud/src/test/scala/org/apache/spark/SparkContextSuite.scala), so no unique resolution exists; the record is rejected rather than resolved to whichever the index happened to see first; collector path_resolution: unresolved-bytecode-only
rejections.expected_detail_note: The detail is the sub-reason AAP 0.5.4 requires a rejection to carry, and it is quoted in full because ambiguous_source_resolution's whole value is that it names the collision rather than the count: a reader who cannot see which two files claimed the key cannot check the rejection. A test may assert the class exactly and the detail by its distinguishing substrings below rather than by full-string equality.
distinguishing_substrings: the class key 'org/apache/spark/SparkContextSuite' is claimed by 2 distinct source files
rejections.why_the_forbidden_substrings_are_recorde: Three committed documents reach this one class, and the class name cannot tell them apart. The forbidden list is the other two routes' key phrases and candidate paths, so an adapter that resolved the wrong key -- or a fixture edited into a different collision -- fails here rather than passing on the class alone. The key phrase is quoted with its closing apostrophe on purpose: org/apache/spark/SparkContext is a prefix of org/apache/spark/SparkContextSuite, so a bare class key would appear in a route it does not belong to.
rejections.record_identity_note: The adapter supplies finding_index, the context members it found -- here method_full_name alone, since this shape carries no method, callee or file member -- and the rule identifier once step 2 has passed; the resolver adds coordinate_field, the raw coordinate under the key class, and the reduced class_key. Enough to find the record in the artifact again, and never the record itself and never a secret value. Note that class holds the raw class_file value: the resolver names the key for what it is resolving, not for the member it was read from, which is why coordinate_field is carried beside it.
rejections.why_not_a_row: There is no single path to put in the row. path is never absent from a row and the field takes one value, so a record with two candidates has no valid row representation -- and the alternatives each hide something: dropping it loses the record, picking one invents a fact, and emitting two would double the record. Counting it under a named class keeps it visible and keeps the arithmetic honest.
rejections.why_this_route_earns_its_own_document: That ambiguity is not confined to main trees, and that the class is decided by what this run's index found rather than by what the collector failed to find: the defective record carries no collector path at all and is still the ambiguous class rather than the unresolvable one.
rejections.contributes_no_severity_literal: The rejected record is never fed to the severity tally, so nothing from it reaches severity-map.md. That document reports literals against the rows the dataset contains, and this record contributes none. It carries no severity literal in any case.
rejections.contributes_no_path_kind: The record produced no path, so it contributes to no path_kind_* counter and to non_filesystem_paths not at all. It does contribute to rule_id_from_rule_id, coordinate_from_class_file and collector_explanation_present, because it reached those steps before being rejected.

behaviours_not_exercised_by_this_fixture.why_absent: every record here passes steps 1 to 3 and carries an integer start_line, so the path step is the only thing that decides any record's outcome

behaviours_not_exercised_by_this_fixture.why_absent: every record here carries a real class-file coordinate, so unknown_class_sentinel_records is 0 and no record reaches the absent-coordinate branch
